xBRIEFInfo.description: Single story for #3206: UAT Shell fail-open residuals via curl/wget/xxd/openssl (authz grants + kill-switch)

plan.title: sec(authz): UAT Shell fail-open residuals — downloaders/decoders plant grants + kill-switch (#3206)

narratives.Description: After #3186, UAT PreToolUse Shell still allows curl/wget/xxd/openssl to plant .deft/authz grants or .deft-directive-disable because INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS and hasKillSwitchShellWrite omit downloaders/decoders and destination flag parsing. Single story closes both HIGH findings.
narratives.Overview:
## Findings
1. HIGH: curl/wget/xxd/openssl plant .deft/authz/** via -o/--output/-O/-out; classifyShellAuthzOps empty; shell-op-unclassifiable allow; forged grant unlocks Write/push/PR/merge.
2. HIGH: curl -o .deft-directive-disable (and peers) bypass hasKillSwitchShellWrite (redirects-only).

## Fix
- packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts: extend indirect write / kill-switch detection for downloaders/decoders + destination flags.
- Fail-closed under active UAT for .deft/authz/** and kill-switch basenames.
- Tests: fixtures for each residual; literal echo redirect still settings deny; forged grant does not unlock Write.
- CHANGELOG security note.

Related: #3186, #3110, #3039
narratives.UserStory: As an operator running UAT with PreToolUse Shell hooks, I want downloaders and decoders that target authz grants or the Directive kill-switch to be denied without a human grant, so that residual fail-open paths after #3186 cannot bypass Wave 1 human-approval.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts: add curl/wget/xxd/openssl to INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS (or equivalent); parse -o/--output/-O/-out destinations; fail-closed under UAT when destination is under .deft/authz/**. 2. Extend hasKillSwitchShellWrite (or peer) so downloader destinations naming kill-switch basenames (e.g. .deft-directive-disable) classify as settings deny under UAT. 3. packages/core/src/authz/classify.test.ts (+ incident-regression if needed): residual cmds under active UAT deny; echo redirect kill-switch still denied; forged grant path does not unlock Write. 4. CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] security for #3206; brief docs note if an authz security surface exists. 5. Verify: npm test -w @deftai/directive-core -- --run authz/classify. Pre-pr, PR, review-cycle, drive-to merge-ready, scope:complete, close #3206.

items.title: Downloader/decoder authz-dir write deny under UAT

narrative.Acceptance: Given active UAT with PreToolUse Shell, when curl/wget/xxd/openssl write or decode to a .deft/authz/** destination via common -o/--output/-O/-out forms, then the op is denied (not shell-op-unclassifiable allow).

items.title: Downloader kill-switch plant deny under UAT

narrative.Acceptance: Given active UAT, when a downloader uses -o/--output/-O to a kill-switch basename (e.g. .deft-directive-disable), then Shell is hard-denied without human grant.
Given the listed bins, when common destination flag forms are used, then classification covers them (not only redirects).

items.title: Regression tests + literal redirect still denied

narrative.Acceptance: Given the test suite, when residual fixtures run under active UAT, each finding is denied; literal echo redirect kill-switch remains settings deny; forged grant does not unlock Write.
Given PR, CHANGELOG [Unreleased] cites #3206 security; review-cycle clean; merge-ready; scope:complete; #3206 closable.
